dimensions.assessment: Affects federal courts, judges, litigants, media organizations, witnesses, and the public observing federal proceedings.
dimensions.evidence: permit the photographing, electronic recording, broadcasting, or televising to the public of any court proceeding

dimensions.assessment: Permits public broadcasting and recording of court proceedings while maintaining due process protections and witness obscuring.
dimensions.evidence: upon the request of any witness (other than a party) in a trial proceeding, the court shall order the face and voice of the witness to be disguised

dimensions.assessment: Requires that accommodations be made without public expense.
dimensions.evidence: A court may require that any accommodations to effectuate this Act be made without public expense.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a comprehensive framework and guidelines across all U.S. district courts, circuit courts of appeals, and the Supreme Court.
dimensions.evidence: appellate court of the United States means any United States circuit court of appeals and the Supreme Court of the United States.

dimensions.assessment: District court media coverage authority sunsets 3 years after enactment, while appellate court provisions operate without a specific statutory sunset.
dimensions.evidence: The authority under this paragraph shall terminate 3 years after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Detailed administrative resource estimates for court implementation of media feeds.
importance_detail.rationale: Grants presiding federal judges the discretion to permit media coverage of federal appellate and district court proceedings, subject to witness protection rules and a 3-year district court sunset.
